title: Interpreting Random Forests: Comparing Surrogate Models and Rule Extraction Methods
abstract: arXiv:2611.19471v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Random forests (RFs) often achieve high prediction performance, but their ensemble structure can be difficult to interpret. Surrogate models and rule extraction methods offer interpretable approximations, yet guidance on selecting an appropriate method for a specific research question remains limited. We compared 12 methods for interpreting RFs, with a decision tree as a prediction-oriented reference, across 11 simulation settings and 67 benchmark datasets for regression and classification. Evaluation addressed prediction and structural similarity to the RF, model complexity, prediction performance, and runtime. Simulations additionally assessed explainability using known effect and noise variables. No method performed best across all objectives. For regression, SLIM provided the strongest general performance for prediction similarity or performance on test data, while a linear model offered a simpler global interpretation of linear ef

translated_title: 解读随机森林：代理模型与规则提取方法的比较
translated_abstract: 随机森林（RF）通常具有很高的预测性能，但其集成结构难以解释。代理模型和规则提取方法可以提供可解释的近似，但针对特定研究问题如何选择合适的方法，相关指导仍然有限。我们在11个模拟设置和67个用于回归与分类任务的基准数据集上，比较了12种解释随机森林的方法，并以决策树作为面向预测的参考。评估内容包括与随机森林的预测及结构相似性、模型复杂度、预测性能和运行时间。模拟实验还利用已知的效应变量和噪声变量额外评估了可解释性。结果显示，没有一种方法能在所有目标上表现最佳。对于回归任务，SLIM在预测相似性或测试数据性能方面提供了最强的综合表现，而线性模型则为线性效应提供了更简单的全局解释。
tldr: 本文系统比较了12种解释随机森林的方法，发现没有一种方法在所有目标上均最优，其中SLIM在回归任务中综合表现最强，为研究者根据具体研究问题选择合适的解释方法提供了指导。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically compares 12 methods for interpreting random forests across simulations and benchmark datasets, finding no universally best method—with SLIM showing the strongest overall performance for regression—thus providing guidance on selecting interpretation methods based on specific research questions.
